question: Which minimum_chrome_version does the extension's service-worker keepalive justify?

quotes.118: Active debugger sessions created using the browser.debugger API now keep the service worker alive.
quotes.116: Active WebSocket connections now extend extension service worker lifetimes.
quotes.110: Extension API calls reset the timers.

relied_on: chrome.debugger session per connected tab (background.ts doConnectTab -> chrome.debugger.attach) keeps the worker alive: Chrome 118
WebSocket to the server bridge from the worker: Chrome 116
other_apis_checked: chrome.* namespaces used in packages/extension/src: storage(local, session, onChanged), tabs, windows, runtime, debugger, downloads, alarms. None of them was checked against a version newer than 118 in a fetched doc.
alarms_note: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/alarms (fetched) now states a 1-second floor; the extension's own 30 s floor (reconnect-policy.ts ALARM_MIN_DELAY_MS) is above it. The version in which the floor was lowered was not found in the fetched page: not verified.
not_verified: No run on Chrome 118 itself; only Chrome 156 was run.
